# azurerm

Stores Terraform state in an [Azure Blob Storage](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-introduction) container. The `key` setting names the blob that holds the state file.

This backend supports state locking and consistency checking with Azure Blob Storage native capabilities.

## Authentication

!> **Warning:**  We recommend using environment variables to supply credentials and other sensitive data. If you use `-backend-config` or hardcode these values directly in your configuration, Terraform will include these values in both the `.terraform` subdirectory and in plan files. Refer to [Credentials and Sensitive Data](/terraform/language/backend#credentials-and-sensitive-data) for details.

The `azurerm` backend needs permission to read and write the state file, and the storage account's blob endpoint address.

Choose one of these authentication methods:

- [Microsoft Entra ID](#microsoft-entra-id) **(Recommended)**
- [SAS Token](#sas-token) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*
- [Access Key](#access-key) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*
- [Access Key Lookup](#access-key-lookup) *(Not recommended for new workloads)*

### Microsoft Entra ID and Access Key Lookup Authentication Types

There are 5 types of Microsoft Entra ID authentication supported, which apply to the Microsoft Entra ID and Access Key Lookup methods.

- OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation **(Recommended)**
  - User Assigned Managed Identity with Federated Credentials **(Recommended)**
  - Service Princial / App Registration with Federated Credentials
- User or System Assigned Managed Identity
  - User Assigned Managed Identity attached to Azure compute instance (agent / runner)
  - System Assigned Managed Identity attached to Azure compute instance (agent / runner)
- Service Principal / App Registration with Client Secret
- Service Principal / App REgistration with Client Certificate
- User Account with Azure CLI only (for local development cycle)

These types can be supplied via inputs or via a pre-authenticated Azure CLI. We cover them in more depth in the following sections.

### Data Plane URI

In most cases, you can infer the data plane URI from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.  Refer to the [storage account overview documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview#standard-endpoints) for more information on the standard endpoints.

If you are using the ['Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/storage/common/storage-account-overview#azure-dns-zone-endpoints-preview), the backend will need to lookup the data plane URI from the management plane. This requires that you set the `lookup_blob_endpoint` configuration option to `true` and the `Reader` role assignment on the storage account.

## Microsoft Entra ID

This method requires a valid Microsoft Entra ID principal and a predictable storage account data plane URI.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `use_azuread_auth` - Set to `true` to use Microsoft Entra ID authentication to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
- `tenant_id` - The tenant ID of the Microsoft Entra ID principal is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Optional Inputs

Use this optional argument to keep provider environment variables out of backend configuration:

- `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` - Set to `true` to ignore provider `ARM_*` defaults. Defaults to `false`. You can also set it with `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE`. This applies to all authentication methods; see the version requirement and details that follow.

The following options apply when [looking up the data plane URI](#data-plane-uri) from the management plane. They are not required when the data plane URI can be inferred from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.

- `lookup_blob_endpoint` - Set to `true` to lookup the storage account data plane URI from the management plane. This is required if you are using the 'Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature. Defaults to `false`. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT` environment variable.
- `subscription_id` - The subscription ID of the storage account is required to query the management plane. This is only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
- `resource_group_name` - The resource group name of the storage account is required to query the management plane. This is only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`.

### Select backend environment variables

~> **Version requirement:** Backend-specific `ARM_BACKEND_*` variables and `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` require a Terraform 1.17 build that includes this feature. Terraform 1.16 does not support them.

The **backend** stores Terraform's record of your resources, called state. The **provider** creates and updates the resources. They do not have to use the same Azure identity or tenant (Microsoft Entra directory).

Use `ARM_BACKEND_*` variables when you want different credentials or settings for state access. For example, keep the state identity's permissions limited to the storage container, while the provider identity manages resources. The state account can also belong to a different subscription or tenant.

`ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID` selects the backend identity; `ARM_CLIENT_ID` selects the provider identity. The full set of supported names is in [Configuration Variables](#configuration-variables). These variables do not grant permissions or change provider authentication.

#### Share settings by default

In non-strict mode, override only what differs. Each backend setting uses the first available value:

1. Explicit backend configuration, including `-backend-config`.
1. The setting's `ARM_BACKEND_*` variable.
1. Its existing `ARM_*` variable.
1. Supported job-level variables, then the setting's default.

Empty strings are skipped. Boolean `false` is a value, not an omission: `ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC="false"` overrides `ARM_USE_OIDC="true"`.

For example, the non-strict workflows share OIDC settings and set only the backend client and tenant IDs. Azure Pipelines also sets a separate backend service connection ID.

#### Use strict mode to separate authentication settings

Strict mode is useful when the backend and provider use different authentication methods. For example, the provider might use a client secret while the backend uses OpenID Connect (OIDC). Without strict mode, the backend can read the provider's `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` and try the wrong method.

Set `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE="true"` to ignore provider `ARM_*` variables. This cleanly separates the environment settings, but requires more inputs: supply every setting the backend needs with `ARM_BACKEND_*` variables or explicit backend configuration. For example, the strict OIDC examples set `ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC` and `ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD` instead of sharing the provider flags.

You can also set `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` in backend configuration. Explicit `true` or `false` overrides the control environment variable, even if that variable is invalid. There is no generic control alias.

Strict mode still allows GitHub and Azure Pipelines job-level token request inputs, so neither platform needs manual token copying. Azure Pipelines still needs the backend service connection ID. An existing Azure CLI login is not a fallback unless you enable `use_cli` or `ARM_BACKEND_USE_CLI`.

Managed identity and Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) workload identity also require opt-in. Enabling AKS workload identity allows its standard `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, and `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE` inputs.

Strict mode controls environment defaults, not authentication priority or credential validation. Each argument is still resolved separately. A direct value does not disable a configured file path; direct client IDs, client secrets, and OIDC tokens must match their file contents when both are supplied.

#### Supply settings for each job

Terraform saves explicit backend configuration in `.terraform` and plan files, but not environment-derived settings or credentials. Supply fresh credentials for each job. If you enable strict mode through its environment variable, set it for every init, plan, and apply command; otherwise the backend returns to non-strict mode.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

The recommended data plane role assignment required for this method is:

- `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the storage account container (Recommended for least privilege)

The recommended management plane role assignments required for this method are:

- `Reader` on the storage account *(Only required if `lookup_blob_endpoint` is set to `true`)*

### Microsoft Entra ID with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation

OpenID Connect (OIDC) lets a workflow request short-lived credentials instead of storing a client secret. These examples use the `Azure/azapi` provider to manage a resource group and the built-in `azurerm` backend to store state. The AzureRM provider is not required.

Choose one example for your continuous integration (CI) platform. Non-strict mode shares settings and needs fewer inputs; strict mode keeps backend authentication settings separate. Each example is complete; do not combine them.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_oidc` - Set to `true` to use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration or User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

<a id="example-configuration-for-github"></a>
<a id="github-actions-with-one-backend-and-provider-identity"></a>

#### GitHub Actions with separate identities in non-strict mode

This example uses OIDC for two identities in different tenants. Non-strict mode shares the authentication settings; only the backend client and tenant IDs differ.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with backend-specific environment variable support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Configure a federated identity credential so each identity trusts this GitHub workflow. Match the workflow's actual token subject exactly, including any organization-specific format, and use the `api://AzureADTokenExchange` audience.

##### Configure workflow variables

Create the following GitHub Actions repository variables. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Repository variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_TENANT_ID` | Provider identity's tenant ID |
| `AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Provider subscription for the example resources |
| `AZAPI_CLIENT_ID` | Provider identity's client ID |
| `STATE_TENANT_ID` | Backend identity's separate tenant ID |
| `STATE_CLIENT_ID` | Backend identity's client ID |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version with backend-specific environment variable support |

The backend accesses the state blob directly, so it does not need `ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, even for another subscription. If you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint` to look up the storage address, also supply the state subscription and resource group and grant `Reader` on the storage account.

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the workflow supplies the storage location at initialization. Authentication comes from environment variables. The resource block describes a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the workflow

Save this as `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml`. `init` connects to state storage and installs the provider; `plan` saves proposed changes to `tfplan`. Both steps use GitHub's token request inputs automatically. Only the backend client and tenant IDs need separate values.

```yaml
name: Plan with separate Azure identities

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # Provider identity and shared authentication flags.
      ARM_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      # Override only the backend identity; other settings use fallback.
      ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_TENANT_ID }}

      # Non-secret storage location passed during initialization.
      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_CONTAINER_NAME }}
      STATE_KEY: ${{ vars.STATE_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ vars.TERRAFORM_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Initialize backend
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform init -input=false `
            "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

      - name: Plan
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
```

Commit both files and run the workflow manually in GitHub Actions. It creates a plan, not Azure resources. For an apply job, supply the same identity settings and storage location with fresh job credentials. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config`, and protect saved plans as sensitive data.

<a id="github-actions-with-separate-backend-and-provider-identities"></a>

#### GitHub Actions with separate identities in strict mode

This example uses OIDC for two identities in different tenants and subscriptions. Strict mode keeps provider environment settings out of backend authentication, so the backend needs its own identity and authentication flags.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with backend-specific environment variable support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container. Add `Reader` on the storage account only if you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint` to look up its blob endpoint.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Configure a federated identity credential so each identity trusts this GitHub workflow. Match the workflow's actual token subject exactly, including any organization-specific format, and use the `api://AzureADTokenExchange` audience.

##### Configure workflow variables

Create the following GitHub Actions repository variables. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Repository variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_TENANT_ID` | Provider identity's tenant ID |
| `AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Provider subscription for the example resources |
| `AZAPI_CLIENT_ID` | Provider identity's client ID |
| `STATE_TENANT_ID` | Backend identity's separate tenant ID |
| `STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` | Backend subscription containing the state account |
| `STATE_CLIENT_ID` | Backend identity's client ID |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version with backend-specific environment variable support |

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the workflow supplies the storage location at initialization. Authentication comes from environment variables. The resource block describes a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the workflow

Save this as `.github/workflows/terraform-plan.yml`. `init` connects to state storage and installs the provider; `plan` saves proposed changes to `tfplan`. Both steps enable strict mode and use GitHub's token request inputs automatically.

```yaml
name: Plan with separate Azure identities in strict mode

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE: "true"

      # Provider identity for the resource tenant and subscription.
      ARM_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.AZAPI_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"

      # Backend identity for the separate state tenant and subscription.
      ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_TENANT_ID }}
      ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID }}
      ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.STATE_CLIENT_ID }}
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      # Non-secret storage location passed during initialization.
      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME }}
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: ${{ vars.STATE_CONTAINER_NAME }}
      STATE_KEY: ${{ vars.STATE_KEY }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@v3
        with:
          terraform_version: ${{ vars.TERRAFORM_VERSION }}
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Initialize backend
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform init -input=false `
            "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
            "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

      - name: Plan
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
          $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

          terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
```

Commit both files and run the workflow manually in GitHub Actions. It creates a plan, not Azure resources. For an apply job, enable strict mode again, supply the same identity settings and storage location, and grant `id-token: write`. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config`, and protect saved plans as sensitive data.

<a id="example-configuration-for-azure-devops"></a>
<a id="azure-pipelines-with-one-backend-and-provider-identity"></a>

#### Azure Pipelines with separate identities in non-strict mode

This example uses two service connections, which let Azure Pipelines authenticate to Azure. Each uses workload identity federation instead of a stored secret. The connections target different tenants and subscriptions. Non-strict mode shares authentication flags and job token inputs; only the backend identity and connection IDs differ.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with backend-specific environment variable support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Create two Azure Resource Manager service connections using workload identity federation. Authorize both for this pipeline and match each identity's federated credential to its connection.
1. Install the [Terraform extension from Microsoft DevLabs](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-devlabs.custom-terraform-tasks) in your Azure DevOps organization to use `TerraformInstaller@1`.

##### Configure pipeline variables

Create these Azure Pipelines variables. Enter service connection names; the tasks obtain their IDs. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Pipeline variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Provider connection name for the resource tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Backend connection name for the separate state tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version with backend-specific environment variable support |

The backend accesses the state blob directly, so it does not need `ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`, even for another subscription. If you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint` to look up the storage address, also supply the state subscription and resource group and grant `Reader` on the storage account.

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the pipeline supplies the storage location at initialization. Authentication comes from environment variables. The resource block describes a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the pipeline

Save this as `azure-pipelines.yml`. `init` connects to state storage and installs the provider using the state connection. `plan` uses the provider connection and restores three backend identity settings from the first task. Shared flags and the job's `System.AccessToken` handle OIDC authentication.

```yaml
trigger: none

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
  - checkout: self

  - task: TerraformInstaller@1
    displayName: "[Terraform] Install Terraform"
    inputs:
      terraformVersion: $(TERRAFORM_VERSION)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Initialize backend"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Initialization needs only the state identity.
        $clientId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $tenantId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $connectionId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $clientId
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $tenantId
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $connectionId

        terraform init -input=false `
          "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

        # Pass only non-secret backend identity metadata to the plan task.
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_CLIENT_ID]$clientId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_TENANT_ID]$tenantId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID]$connectionId"
    env:
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: $(STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME)
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: $(STATE_CONTAINER_NAME)
      STATE_KEY: $(STATE_KEY)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Plan"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Provider identity comes from this task's service connection.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
    env:
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

      # Only the backend identity and service connection differ.
      ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID: $(STATE_CLIENT_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID: $(STATE_TENANT_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID)
```

Commit both files, create an Azure Pipeline from the YAML file, and run it manually. It creates a plan, not Azure resources. For an apply job, repeat the connection setup and identity settings, with its own `System.AccessToken` and the same storage location. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config`, and protect saved plans as sensitive data.

Both connections refresh OIDC tokens automatically. Avoid unrelated credential variables in this non-strict example: the backend can read generic `ARM_*` values.

<a id="azure-pipelines-with-separate-backend-and-provider-identities"></a>

#### Azure Pipelines with separate identities in strict mode

This example uses two service connections, which let Azure Pipelines authenticate to Azure. Each uses workload identity federation instead of a stored secret. The connections target different tenants and subscriptions. Strict mode keeps provider environment settings out of backend authentication, so the backend needs its own identity and authentication flags.

##### Prepare your environment

1. Use a Terraform 1.17 build with backend-specific environment variable support.
1. Create the state storage account and container before running Terraform. Grant the backend identity `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the container. Add `Reader` on the storage account only if you enable `lookup_blob_endpoint` to look up its blob endpoint.
1. Grant the provider identity permission to manage the example resource group in the provider subscription.
1. Create two Azure Resource Manager service connections using workload identity federation. Authorize both for this pipeline and match each identity's federated credential to its connection.
1. Install the [Terraform extension from Microsoft DevLabs](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-devlabs.custom-terraform-tasks) in your Azure DevOps organization to use `TerraformInstaller@1`.

##### Configure pipeline variables

Create these Azure Pipelines variables. Enter service connection names; the tasks obtain their IDs. `STATE_KEY` is the state blob name, such as `example.terraform.tfstate`, not an access key.

| Pipeline variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Provider connection name for the resource tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION` | Backend connection name for the separate state tenant and subscription |
| `STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME` | Existing state storage account name |
| `STATE_CONTAINER_NAME` | Existing state container name |
| `STATE_KEY` | State blob name |
| `TERRAFORM_VERSION` | Terraform 1.17 version with backend-specific environment variable support |

##### Create the Terraform configuration

Save this as `main.tf` in the repository root. The empty backend block uses [partial configuration](/terraform/language/backend#partial-configuration): the pipeline supplies the storage location at initialization. Authentication comes from environment variables. The resource block describes a resource group in the provider's subscription.

```hcl
terraform {
  required_version = ">= 1.17.0"

  required_providers {
    azapi = {
      source  = "Azure/azapi"
      version = "~> 2.0"
    }
  }

  backend "azurerm" {}
}

provider "azapi" {}

data "azapi_client_config" "current" {}

resource "azapi_resource" "example" {
  type      = "Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups@2024-03-01"
  name      = "example-resources"
  location  = "westeurope"
  parent_id = "/subscriptions/${data.azapi_client_config.current.subscription_id}"
  body      = {}
}
```

##### Run the pipeline

Save this as `azure-pipelines.yml`. `init` connects to state storage and installs the provider using the state connection. `plan` uses the provider connection while keeping the state identity for backend access. Both tasks run in the same job and directory, with strict mode enabled in each.

```yaml
trigger: none

pool:
  vmImage: ubuntu-latest

steps:
  - checkout: self

  - task: TerraformInstaller@1
    displayName: "[Terraform] Install Terraform"
    inputs:
      terraformVersion: $(TERRAFORM_VERSION)

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Initialize backend"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # Initialize state with the backend service connection.
        $clientId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $tenantId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $connectionId = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID
        $subscriptionId = az account show --query id --output tsv

        $env:ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID = $clientId
        $env:ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID = $tenantId
        $env:ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = $subscriptionId
        $env:ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $connectionId

        terraform init -input=false `
          "-backend-config=storage_account_name=$env:STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=container_name=$env:STATE_CONTAINER_NAME" `
          "-backend-config=key=$env:STATE_KEY"

        # Pass only non-secret identity metadata to the next task.
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_CLIENT_ID]$clientId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_TENANT_ID]$tenantId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID]$subscriptionId"
        Write-Host "##vso[task.setvariable variable=STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID]$connectionId"
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE: "true"
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)

      STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME: $(STATE_STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME)
      STATE_CONTAINER_NAME: $(STATE_CONTAINER_NAME)
      STATE_KEY: $(STATE_KEY)

      ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD: "true"

  - task: AzureCLI@2
    displayName: "[Terraform] Plan"
    inputs:
      azureSubscription: $(AZAPI_SERVICE_CONNECTION)
      scriptType: pscore
      scriptLocation: inlineScript
      visibleAzLogin: false
      inlineScript: |
        $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
        $PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true

        # The provider uses this task's connection; state uses the earlier one.
        $env:ARM_CLIENT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_CLIENT_ID
        $env:ARM_TENANT_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_TENANT_ID
        $env:ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID = az account show --query id --output tsv
        $env:ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID = $env:AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID

        terraform plan -input=false -out=tfplan
    env:
      ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE: "true"
      SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN: $(System.AccessToken)
      ARM_USE_OIDC: "true"

      # Restore the backend identity, not credentials from the previous task.
      ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID: $(STATE_CLIENT_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID: $(STATE_TENANT_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID: $(STATE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID: $(STATE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID)
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC: "true"
      ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD: "true"
```

Commit both files, create an Azure Pipeline from the YAML file, and run it manually. It creates a plan, not Azure resources. For an apply job, repeat the connection setup, identity settings, strict-mode control, and storage location, with its own `System.AccessToken`. Keep credentials out of `-backend-config`, and protect saved plans as sensitive data.

Both connections refresh OIDC tokens automatically. `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` keeps the backend on the state connection from the first task. Strict mode does not reuse the provider task's connection ID.

### Microsoft Entra ID with Compute Attached Managed Identity

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_msi` - Set to `true` to use the managed identity to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.

#### Optional Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are optional for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This is not required for System Assigned Managed Identity. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_msi              = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_MSI` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable. Not required for System Assigned Managed Identity.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Azure CLI

You must have a pre-authenticated Azure CLI session using any supported method.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_cli` - Set to `true` to use the Azure CLI session authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_CLI` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_cli              = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_CLI` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable. Azure CLI will fallback to use the connected tenant ID if not supplied.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Client Secret

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

#### Required Inputs

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
- `client_secret` - The client secret of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_secret        = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

### Microsoft Entra ID with Client Certificate

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility only, do not use it for any new workloads.

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation as a more secure approach.

#### Required Inputs

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
- `client_certificate_path` - The path to the client certificate bundle is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
- `client_certificate_password` - The password for the client certificate bundle is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.

#### Example Configuration

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_azuread_auth            = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_certificate_path     = "/path/to/bundle.pfx"                   # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
    client_certificate_password = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.
    storage_account_name        = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name              = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                         = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## Access Key

This method requires you find the Access Key for the storage account and supply it to the backend configuration.

The Access Key is then used to directly authenticate to the storage account data plane.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `access_key` - The Access Key of the storage account is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

There are no role assignments required on the storage account for this method as the Access Key is used to authenticate to the data plane.

### Example Configuration

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Consider using OIDC as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    access_key           = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789..."  # Can also be set via `ARM_ACCESS_KEY` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                                 # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                                  # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                   # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## SAS Token

This method requires you generate a SAS Token for the storage account container or blob and supply it to the backend configuration.

The SAS Token is then used to directly authenticate to the storage account data plane.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `sas_token` - The SAS Token for the storage account container or blob is required to authenticate to the storage account data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_SAS_TOKEN` environment variable.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Storage Account Required Permissions

The SAS Token requires `write` and `list` permissions on the container or blob.

### Example Configuration

~> **Warning!** This method requires you to manage and rotate a secret. Consider using OIDC as a more secure approach.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    sas_token            = "abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789..."  # Can also be set via `ARM_SAS_TOKEN` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                                 # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                                  # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                   # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## Access Key Lookup

This method requires a valid Microsoft Entra ID principal and is a fallback for when Microsoft Entra ID authentication cannot be used on the storage account data plane.

This method queries the management plane to get the storage account Access Key and then uses that Access Key to authenticate to the storage account data plane. It requires elevated permissions on the storage account.

Terraform retains this method for backwards compatibility, we do not recommend it for new workloads.

### Required Configuration Options

The following configuration options are always required for this method:

- `tenant_id` - The tenant ID of the Microsoft Entra ID principal is required to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
- `subscription_id` - The subscription ID of the storage account is required to query the management plane. If using Azure CLI, this can be inferred from the CLI session. This can also be set via the `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
- `resource_group_name` - The resource group name of the storage account is required to query the management plane.
- `storage_account_name` - The name of the storage account to write the state file blob to.
- `container_name` - The name of the storage account container to write the state file blob to.
- `key` - The name of the blob within the storage account container to write the state file to.

### Optional Configuration Options

The optional `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` argument also applies to this method. It defaults to `false` and can be set with `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE`. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for the Terraform 1.17 requirement and precedence rules.

These optional configuration options apply when [looking up the data plane URI](#data-plane-uri) from the management plane. They are not required when the data plane URI can be inferred from the `storage_account_name` and `container_name`.

- `lookup_blob_endpoint` - Set to `true` to lookup the storage account data plane URI from the management plane. This is required if you are using the 'Azure DNS zone endpoints' feature. Defaults to `false`. This value can also be sourced from the `ARM_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT` environment variable.

### Storage Account Required Role Assignments

The recommended data plane role assignment required for this method is:

- `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on the storage account container (Recommended for least privilege)

The recommended management plane role assignments required for this method are:

- `Reader` on the storage account
- `Storage Account Key Operator Service Role` on the storage account

### Access Key Lookup with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation

OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation is the recommended method for this scenario.

#### Required Configuration Options

The following additional configuration options are always required for this sub-type:

- `use_oidc` - Set to `true` to use OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
- `client_id` - The client ID of the Microsoft Entra ID Service Principal / App Registration or User Assigned Managed Identity is required to authenticate to the storage account management and data plane. This can also be set via the `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.

<a id="example-configuration-for-github-1"></a>

#### GitHub Actions with access key lookup

GitHub's job-level token request environment variables are automatically found in both modes. Refer to [GitHub Actions with separate identities in strict mode](#github-actions-with-separate-identities-in-strict-mode) for separate backend and provider authentication.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_oidc             = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id      = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

<a id="example-configuration-for-azure-devops-1"></a>

#### Azure Pipelines with access key lookup

Azure DevOps job-level token request variables are automatically found in both modes. Supply `ado_pipeline_service_connection_id` or one of its supported environment aliases; strict mode permits only the backend-specific alias. Refer to [Azure Pipelines with separate identities in non-strict mode](#azure-pipelines-with-separate-identities-in-non-strict-mode) for the service connection setup.

```hcl
terraform {
  backend "azurerm" {
    use_oidc                         = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    ado_pipeline_service_connection_id = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID` environment variable.
    tenant_id                        = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    subscription_id                  = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                        = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    resource_group_name              = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name             = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name                   = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                              = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

```hcl
    subscription_id             = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` environment variable.
    client_id                   = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    client_certificate_path     = "/path/to/bundle.pfx"                   # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` environment variable.
    client_certificate_password = "************************************"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` environment variable.
    resource_group_name  = "StorageAccount-ResourceGroup"          # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"resource_group_name=<resource group name>"` in the `init` command.
    storage_account_name        = "abcd1234"                              # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"storage_account_name=<storage account name>"` in the `init` command.
    container_name              = "tfstate"                               # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"container_name=<container name>"` in the `init` command.
    key                         = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # Can be passed via `-backend-config=`"key=<blob key name>"` in the `init` command.
  }
}
```

## terraform_remote_state Data Source

To use the `terraform_remote_state` data source with the `azurerm` backend, you must use the exact same configuration as you would for the `backend` block in your configuration.

For example to use [Direct Microsoft Entra ID authentication with OpenID Connect / Workload identity federation for GitHub](#microsoft-entra-id-with-openid-connect--workload-identity-federation) you would use the following configuration:

```hcl
data "terraform_remote_state" "foo" {
  backend = "azurerm"
  config = {
    use_oidc             = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_OIDC` environment variable.
    use_azuread_auth     = true                                    # Can also be set via `ARM_USE_AZUREAD` environment variable.
    tenant_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_TENANT_ID` environment variable.
    client_id            = "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"  # Can also be set via `ARM_CLIENT_ID` environment variable.
    storage_account_name = "abcd1234"                              # There is not environment variable support for this input.
    container_name       = "tfstate"                               # There is not environment variable support for this input.
    key                  = "prod.terraform.tfstate"                # There is not environment variable support for this input.
  }
}
```

## Configuration Variables

!> **Warning:**  We recommend using environment variables to supply credentials and other sensitive data. If you use `-backend-config` or hardcode these values directly in your configuration, Terraform will include these values in both the `.terraform` subdirectory and in plan files. Refer to [Credentials and Sensitive Data](/terraform/language/backend#credentials-and-sensitive-data) for details.

For more information on when each of these configuration settings is required, refer to the previous sections of this page.

The following configuration options are supported. Where multiple environment names are listed, the first non-empty value wins after explicit configuration. Backend-specific `ARM_BACKEND_*` alternatives require Terraform 1.17. Strict mode excludes generic `ARM_*` defaults but retains GitHub and Azure Pipelines job-level token request inputs. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for authentication requirements and other opt-in behavior.

* `backend_environment_variable_strict_mode` - (Optional) Set to `true` to prevent fallback to provider environment defaults. Defaults to `false`. Can also be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLE_STRICT_MODE`; there is no generic control alias. Explicit configuration, including `false`, takes precedence. Requires Terraform 1.17 with backend-specific environment variable support. Refer to [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables) for authentication and persistence rules.

* `storage_account_name` - (Required) The Name of [the Storage Account](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/storage_account).

* `container_name` - (Required) The Name of [the Storage Container](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/azurerm/latest/docs/resources/storage_container) within the Storage Account.

* `key` - (Required) The name of the Blob used to retrieve/store Terraform's State file inside the Storage Container.

* `environment` - (Optional) The Azure environment to use. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_ENVIRONMENT` or `ARM_ENVIRONMENT`. Possible values are `public`, `china`, and `usgovernment`. Defaults to `public`.

* `metadata_host` - (Optional) The hostname of the Azure Metadata Service, such as `management.azure.com`, used to obtain a custom Azure environment. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_METADATA_HOSTNAME`, `ARM_METADATA_HOSTNAME`, or `ARM_METADATA_HOST`.

* `lookup_blob_endpoint` - (Optional) Set to `true` to look up the storage account data plane URI from the management plane. Defaults to `false`. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT` or `ARM_USE_DNS_ZONE_ENDPOINT`.

* `snapshot` - (Optional) Set to `true` to snapshot the state blob before use. Defaults to `false`. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_SNAPSHOT` or `ARM_SNAPSHOT`.

* `tenant_id` - (Optional) The tenant ID of the backend identity. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_TENANT_ID` or `ARM_TENANT_ID`.

* `use_azuread_auth` - (Optional) Use Microsoft Entra ID authentication for the storage account data plane. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_USE_AZUREAD` or `ARM_USE_AZUREAD`.

* `subscription_id` - (Optional) The storage account's subscription ID, required for management-plane authentication. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_SUBSCRIPTION_ID` or `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID`. Direct Microsoft Entra ID storage access without management-plane lookup does not require it.

* `resource_group_name` - (Optional) The Name of the Resource Group in which the Storage Account exists required for management plane authentication.

* `access_key` - (Optional) The access key for [Access Key](#access-key) authentication to the storage account data plane. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_ACCESS_KEY` or `ARM_ACCESS_KEY`.

* `sas_token` - (Optional) The token for [SAS Token](#sas-token) authentication to the storage account data plane. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_SAS_TOKEN` or `ARM_SAS_TOKEN`.

* `use_cli` - (Optional) Set to `true` to use an existing Azure CLI login for authentication. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_USE_CLI` or `ARM_USE_CLI`. Defaults to `true` in non-strict mode and `false` in strict mode. Strict mode requires explicit configuration or `ARM_BACKEND_USE_CLI` to enable it.

* `use_oidc` - (Optional) Set to `true` to use OpenID Connect / workload identity federation. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_USE_OIDC` or `ARM_USE_OIDC`.

* `client_id` - (Optional) The client ID of the backend identity. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID` or `ARM_CLIENT_ID`.

* `ado_pipeline_service_connection_id` - (Optional) The Azure DevOps service connection ID for OIDC authentication. Environment precedence is `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`, `ARM_ADO_PIPELINE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`, `ARM_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`, then `AZURESUBSCRIPTION_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`. Strict mode uses only `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_AZURE_SERVICE_CONNECTION_ID`. The generic legacy aliases remain available in non-strict mode.

* `oidc_request_url` - (Optional) The URL from which to request an OIDC token. Environment precedence is `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_REQUEST_URL`, `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_URL`, `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL`, then `SYSTEM_OIDCREQUESTURI`. Strict mode omits `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_URL` but retains both platforms' job-level defaults, in the same order. Azure Pipelines authentication still requires a backend service connection ID.

* `oidc_request_token` - (Optional) The bearer token for the OIDC token request. Environment precedence is `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN`, `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN`, `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`, then `SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN`. Strict mode omits `ARM_OIDC_REQUEST_TOKEN` but retains both platforms' job-level defaults, in the same order. Azure Pipelines authentication still requires a backend service connection ID.

* `oidc_token` - (Optional) The ID token for OpenID Connect authentication, for advanced scenarios or third-party integrations. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_TOKEN` or `ARM_OIDC_TOKEN`.

* `oidc_token_file_path` - (Optional) The path to a file containing an OpenID Connect ID token, for advanced scenarios or third-party integrations. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE_PATH` or `ARM_OIDC_TOKEN_FILE_PATH`.

* `use_aks_workload_identity` - (Optional) Set to `true` to use AKS workload identity. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_USE_AKS_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY` or `ARM_USE_AKS_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY`. Enabling it permits the native AKS identity inputs described in [Select backend environment variables](#select-backend-environment-variables).

* `use_msi` - (Optional) Set to `true` to use a compute-attached managed identity. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_USE_MSI` or `ARM_USE_MSI`.

* `msi_endpoint` - (Optional) A custom managed identity endpoint. Terraform determines the endpoint automatically when omitted. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_MSI_ENDPOINT` or `ARM_MSI_ENDPOINT`.

* `client_id_file_path` - (Optional) The path to a file containing the client ID. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_ID_FILE_PATH` or `ARM_CLIENT_ID_FILE_PATH`.

* `client_certificate_password` - (Optional) The client certificate password. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD` or `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`.

* `client_certificate_path` - (Optional) The path to the PFX client certificate file. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH` or `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE_PATH`.

* `client_certificate` - (Optional) A base64-encoded PKCS#12 client certificate bundle. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE` or `ARM_CLIENT_CERTIFICATE`.

* `client_secret` - (Optional) The client secret of the service principal. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_SECRET` or `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET`.

* `client_secret_file_path` - (Optional) The path to a file containing the client secret. Can be sourced from `ARM_BACKEND_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE_PATH` or `ARM_CLIENT_SECRET_FILE_PATH`.
